newsitem.title: USA: Sony names new management team for studio.
newsitem.headline: Sony names new management team for studio.

text.p: Sony Corp. Tuesday named a new management team for its money-losing Sony Pictures unit, and for the first time moved a Japanese executive into a top job at the studio.
The announcement comes after months of management turmoil that culminated last week in the resignation of Alan Levine as president of the troubled studio.

The Japanese electronics giant said John Calley, President and Chief Operating Officer for United Artists Pictures, will join Sony Pictures Entertainment as president and chief operating officer, effective in early November.
Jeff Sagansky, executive vice president for Sony Corp. of America, will join Sony Pictures as co-president with responsibility for the management of the company under Calley.

Masayuki Nozoe, executive vice president for Sony Corp. of America, will become executive vice president for Sony Pictures, marking the first time a Japanese executive will play an active role in Sony's studio operations.
Sony said Calley will focus particularly on the motion picture business and home video, with Sagansky focusing on television activities and international business.
Nozoe will be responsible for Sony cross-company business development, liaison with corporate headquarters, and technology management. All three executives will be based in Los Angeles.

"These are very important appointments for Sony Pictures Entertainment," said Nobuyuki Idei, Sony Corp. President and Chief Operating Officer. "John's vast experience and proven track record in the industry will be a tremendous asset to Sony."

Calley replaces Levine, who stepped down last week in the latest in a series of management changes at the studio. Last month, Levine fired studio boss Mark Canton after several Sony films flopped at the box office.

Earlier this summer, Marc Platt, president of Sony's TriStar Pictures, left to take a job at Universal Pictures and Lisa Henson, president of Sony's Columbia Pictures, stepped down to form her own production company.
In addition, Sid Ganis, the head of Sony Pictures marketing unit, also stepped down.
The turmoil has prompted many to suggest Sony may sell the troubled studio after amassing billions of dollars in losses since it acquired it in 1989 for $3.4 billion.
But Idei said Sony intends to remain in Hollywood.

"This team represents a new vision and new direction for the studio," Idei said. "We are committed to the growth and success of Sony Pictures Entertainment and to making Sony the global entertainment and communications company of the future."
As head of Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc.'s United Artists studio, Calley played a key role in the revitalisation of the studio with hits such as "Goldeneye", "Birdcage" and "Leaving Las Vegas".
Sagansky, a former executive with CBS, now owned by Westinghouse Electric Corp., has been executive vice president since September 1994.
Nozoe has been executive vice president of Sony Corp. of America since February, mainly with responsibilities for new business development.
